As solid as the core gameplay is, Darktide is ultimately an unfinished mess, with numerous promises from Fatshark undelivered to this day. The amount of content from open beta to the full launch is minuscule at best, the game is still riddled with glitches and crashes that have yet to be addressed since the CLOSED BETA from October and communication between Fatshark and players have been incredibly tone-deaf. Have I mentioned that the crafting shop only has 1 out of 4 features finished at launch? The rest are labeled in-game as, "Coming soon."

The only significant addition (aside from 1 new mission, woohoo) AT LAUNCH is the premium cosmetics shop, which had incredibly scummy FOMO (Fear of Missing Out) tactics such as timers, including premium currency packs that are designed so that you will never have the amount you want (which forces players to spend more money). Player backlash forced Fatshark to backpedal on their FOMO and pricing, but they have confirmed to be reintroducing FOMO at a later date sadly.

I do truly enjoy this game's combat and gameplay, but this game is clearly unfinished and absolutely riddled with predatory monetization. Even Fatshark's own game is working against their own updates, as they had to slowly trickle out content from a recent patch over the course of many hours at the time of this writing.
Why the hell is there no solo play 4 years later thats insane. Also the game runs like shit and is 150gbs. Other then these two massive glaring problems its really fun but yknow

Huge step backwards in every way compared to their previous games except graphically. Gameplay is fun but held back by terrible systems, a more predatory form of monetization, annoying timegating, more rng-based weapon systems, no incentive to play on the higher difficulties, crafting materials no longer shared between characters. Anything that isn't the gameplay feels awful to engage with.

It's too repetitive and has no end.
Well the gameplay itself is still fun, but what have happed to the normal list of campaign missions? I mean you can't just launch the game, go through first mission, than launch second etc. Missions are available for limited time and so, you're going to play mission 5, than mission 3, than mission 5 again (because how is it supposed to work? Do I need to have a note of what missions i played?).

Looks super cool and would love to play it, but apparently there is still no single player option and is online only. There is a minimum of 2 people to launch any mission. A single player option is a basic requirement for nearly any rpg-like game so not sure what the thought was behind that one.

Quality co-op title.
Fully cross platform so our group is often made up PC, PS5 and Xbox players.
The graphics are amazing.
Re-use of assets is a clever use of resources.
Runs well. I wouldn't say best optimisation but nothing worth moaning about (I don't use Raytracing as on AMD).
The attention to detail is brilliant.
I can honestly say after the time I've spent playing that this game is made with love.
I'm sure some further content would not do it any harm and would happily pay for it.

Pretty good, and getting better with every update! Solid follow-up to Vermintide with a great 40K atmosphere, and a very satisfying moment to moment gameplay.

Great to be able to cross-play with friends who have the game on console, and since it's on Game Pass, it's a low barrier to trying it out.

Jesper Kyd's soundtrack elevates it all to 11, expect to head bob <3
Buy this for Jesper Kyd: the gameplay is neat & rough around the edges (or incomplete). But the music THE MUSIC: DIVINE.

I've been playing since launch, witnessed all the bugs, countless unfulfilled promises from Fatshark, and apology letters. The game focused on weekly, repetitive contracts that required countless hours of grinding. Obviously after a few hundred hours invested, the gameplay-loop became boring. However, it seems that a few months ago, the game was finally fixed, and the content promised at launch was delivered.
At first, I wouldn't recommend this game, but now it's probably worth purchasing at discounted price.
2025 update: The game is decent, but locking the supposedly "free content update" behind a DLC paywall is the pinnacle of Fatshark's greed. Such a shame.

Intense horde melee/shooter that is best in its class. The developer's "-Tide" games are a master class of this sort of category.

However, this same developer has a well known streak of having a terrible live service model/support. Takes months, or even years for significant updates with little to no communication.

It was a struggling game long ago. An unfinished, rushed mess that you really must love the "-Tide" games to stay.

Now? its robust enough to recommend to pick up and play. Don't expect more than what it has and you may end up pleasantly surprised when the dev eventually decides to develop something to add in their game.

Though again, months or years later.
Core game is fun for a while. But Fatsharks decision to prioritize the cash shop over releasing a feature complete game, makes me hesitant to recommend this game.

An absolute blast wrapped in a ticking time bomb of broken code.
First off, huge thanks to my brother for gifting me this game—the core cooperative gameplay, combat loop, and atmosphere are genuinely incredible. When you drop into a match, the action is top-tier. My PC completely destroys it at 1080p on extreme settings using frame generation, delivering buttery-smooth performance right out of the gate.
The problem is the unmitigated memory leak cancer plaguing this engine.
No matter how high-end your hardware is or how well you brute-force your settings at the start of a session, the game suffers from a severe cumulative degradation loop. Over the course of a mission, background assets and script data fail to flush out, slowly choking your buffers until the frame pacing collapses right before extraction. You are forced to manually restart the entire application just to clear the pipes, acting as an unpaid QA tester for an optimization issue that has persisted for years.
It drives me insane seeing positive reviews brush this under the rug or act like brute-forcing high frame rates on a powerful GPU means the game is fine. Having expensive hardware doesn't excuse lazy optimization or broken garbage collection. If you love visceral combat, the game is great—just be ready to restart your game constantly because the backend architecture is fundamentally rotting from the inside out.

I've never been into 40K. All 40K media is focused on space marines, and I've always thought that space marines looked like toys for 6 year olds. This game is a very different take on the 40K universe, and I now consider it my gateway drug. Its different, because in this game you're not a space marine. You see the 40K universe from the perspective of an Imperial grunt fighting for survival. But none of that would matter if the game wasn't fun, which it is.

The gameplay is very fun. Its a well-executed class-based zombie shooter and slasher in the 40K universe. I think it is an interesting mix of Left 4 Dead and Killing Floor. The graphics are excellent, but even my 3070 RTX and i7 10700K struggle with the settings turned up. Regarding graphics settings, unless you have a brand-new top of the line machine, I recommend turning off ray-tracing and utilizing DLSS or the AMD frame generation to enhance frame rates.

I don't have enough time in game to give an in-depth review, but for now, 8.5/10, will blaspheme the throne again.

I'm giving a positive review because the core gameplay is fun, the graphics are great, the environments interesting, and I get good fps on high settings. It is worth a purchase during a sale, HOWEVER, I do have some big issues with the game. It feels like a downgrade to Vermintide 2. Perhaps the combat is more varied but nearly every system outside of gameplay is worse in my opinion.

The new class overhaul and various quality of life changes saved the game and now the game is a much more enjoyable experience.

I am not a fan of the trend with games at the moment though with releasing in a pretty rough state and then being a full/polished game like nearly a year later, though.

Good setting and art direction marred by greedy in-game pricing, poor optimisation, and extortionate paid character classes ($20 AUD for a new character ontop of a $60 game). The developers are more concerned with marketising the in-game item shop - which is engineered to rotate once every 2 weeks to push FOMO pracitices - rather than providing meaningful changes to improve the player experience. Gameplay is good and fun but lots of features are broken or buggy following minor updates.
Gorb smash. Gorb shoot big boom. Small man become squishy paste under Gorb feet. Gorb make emperor proud. Gorb good Ogryn.

This game launched incredibly broken along with missing key game modes and features. As of two months from launch, those features are still missing, and many bugs are still present.

If this wasn't enough, the core gameplay loop that is oddly lauded as the strongest feature in the game is hamstrung by an equipment system where acquisition and stats are based in hourly/daily RNG. This puts the players experience of the core gameplay entirely at the mercy of random chance, even without the unpredictability of unstable performance issues.

What shifts this seeming negligence into all out contempt is a glitchless, fully functional cosmetic cash shop which was active since launch. This is not a free to play game, nor is it early access from an indie developer just trying to scrape by. This is a premium purchase game launched by an experienced team backed by one of the most wealthy shareholders in the video game market.

This game feels like a con. Even if all these things are eventually fixed, it will never change the absolute swindle it pulled shamelessly to get there. Don't buy this game, ever.
I absolutely abhor the FOMO stupid expensive cosmetic nonsense but the game itself is *FANTASTIC*. Visceral, exciting, a masterclass in environmental design and an absolutely banging soundtrack.

Easily best combat out of any 40k game, and easily up there with one of the smoothest horde shooters. Is an actual horde shooter unlike space marine 2, and unlike space marine 2 enemies take damage and react to your hits. The combat loop is very fast and satisfying, you do a lot of damage, but take it in equal measure. Although some of the guns are hit and miss, melee combat feels great no matter the weapon you use. As far as art style goes it looks fantastic, with the maps looking amazing. Specialists can be easily identified, whether through their silhouette or their unique sound ques. The soundtrack is phenomenal with new tracks being added every new map, which come every couple months. Along with semi regular weapon updates, there is plenty of room for additions due to the massive source material. If you are looking for a fast -paced co op fps this is one of the best possible options and I have yet to find a horde shooter which even comes close to how good this game feels at higher difficulties.

(I'm posting this here, cuzz no one reads DLC reviews) Don't buy the DLC classes unless you REALLY REALLY like the game and are okay with playing a class with a narrower role that only has a handful of semi-unique equipment to use. The DLC classes have so far received no additional unlocks since their respective launches. The DLC classes also lack end game rewards of any kind; the super-hard game mode that exists for the masochists in the community has no rewards for them, the achievement reward track does not have rewards for them, and the new extraction-shooter-esq game mode also does not have rewards for them... The devs have not made *any* comment as to why, and the Discord mods attack you when you bring it up.

I'll update this review if they add any pursuit content for the DLC classes, but it has been nearly a year now for one of them and another class is probably about to be added in Q2/Q3 this year with likely the same problems. I'd like to be surprised but at this point with pretty much any game developer it's just not worth getting my or your hopes up.

I didn't find myself enjoying this game after playing it, but it still has potential to be better, especially if more variety missions and maps were added similar to Deep Rock Galactic and Vermintide 2. Combat is decent but the gameplay itself feels repetitive and boring.

It's not terrible however, since there is still plenty of room for improvement, and not to mention the crashes and disconnects I usually get throughout the game, which has been a huge problem in the game.

Wanted to like the game but sadly loneliness killed me in these dark rooms. The whole game is not that bad at i would say its very well done with gameplay feel. Shooting feels just right and you can feel every bullet that lands on enemy. Melee is also meaty and impactful. Movement with weapons feels very slick and right. Dark coridors and rooms can make you feel clautraphobic and like you in dire situation. Nowhere is safe to land your free time. I wished that the story grabbed me more.

It's a good game. Not a lot of innovation on the bigger points, but there are a lot of thought behind all the minor machanics.
But despite me not being a hardcore fan, it i do get the sense, it's true to the cannon and lore. And you can set up your character with a lot of it, and RP your way through the game.

It's fun, beautiful and despite a lack of innovation on the major areas, it does give you a feel of being a breath of fresh air.
